periodicity.text: The light curve is dominated by a smooth sinusoid with period 0.13149 d (Lomb-Scargle power 0.24); the adopted 1.84082 d is 14.00 x that. The true period is more likely 0.13149 d (pulsation or spots) or 0.26298 d (contact binary), and the 'eclipses' may not be eclipses.

checks: No eclipse at 43 of 91 covered epochs where the 1.84082 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.

writeup: TIC 395085556 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.840823 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.28%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal registered a detection significance of 161.0 in the Box Least Squares search. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 7.6, though the centroid offset of 4.5 arcsec warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, a data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true orbital period may be twice the initial measurement. Despite this open question about the eclipse pattern, the pixel-level confirmation and timing remain unaffected by this systematic effect.
